principles: Never rewrite history: archived evidence MOVES with git mv, it is never edited.
Every intermediate commit must leave a working repo — no flag day.
Read-both before rename: the deprecated identity stays readable while only the canonical one is written.
Prove reversibility before performing an irreversible-feeling step, not after.
Put the one truly irreversible break last, and announce it rather than let it be discovered by failure.
drivers: 7580 git-tracked files and 344 story archives under the state directory — a partial migration orphans audit history other work depends on.
The signature salts are path-independent (verified), so renaming paths is safe for historical signatures; this is what makes the story attemptable at all.
B-cdf6 proved the additive read-both pattern works (core/brand-env.ts), so the mechanism is known rather than invented here.
Operator asked for the full six-item set and said to ignore other in-flight stories; that waives coordination but not evidence preservation.
B-cdf6 lesson: four regressions came from hardcoded DEPRECATED literals inside comparisons, where the CANONICAL name silently failed.

options.name: flag-day-sweep
pros: Fastest: one sweep of find-and-replace plus a single git mv.
Least total commits, easiest to describe.
cons: A half-completed run orphans 344 story archives with no reverse path.
Every intermediate state is a broken repo, so an interruption is unrecoverable without manual surgery.
Provides no place to catch the B-cdf6 comparison-literal class before it ships.

options.name: resolver-first-then-migrate
pros: Read-both resolver lands FIRST, so the codebase operates on either layout and the move becomes reversible.
Rollback is rehearsed on a scratch clone BEFORE the 7580-file move, so the escape hatch provably exists.
Config/manifest renames keep a deprecated-name read path, so teammates and unmigrated projects still load.
The irreversible bin removal is last and gated on a CHANGELOG announcement.
Residue gate is flipped to forbid at the end, so the migration cannot silently regress.
cons: 8 checklist items and many more commits than a flag-day sweep.
The resolver is temporary scaffolding that a later story must eventually remove.
Slower to reach the visible end state.

options.name: subset-skip-state-dir
pros: Lowest risk: do only the config filenames, manifest and package name; skip the state-directory move entirely.
cons: Leaves the single largest and most user-visible inconsistency (.lattice) in place, so the story does not deliver what was asked.
The product reviewer judged that subsetting saves little total risk because the resolver work is the heavy lift either way.
Guarantees a follow-up story to finish the same job, paying the setup cost twice.

rationale: resolver-first-then-migrate is the only option where every intermediate state is a working repo and the heaviest step is reversible before it runs. flag-day-sweep is rejected outright: with 7580 tracked files and 344 archives, an interrupted find-and-replace has no reverse path and would orphan audit history other stories depend on — the one outcome this story must not produce. subset-skip-state-dir was genuinely considered and the product reviewer independently reached the same conclusion I did: it dodges the largest inconsistency while still paying most of the engineering cost, because the read-both resolver is the heavy lift whether or not the directory actually moves. The chosen option costs more commits and leaves temporary scaffolding, which is a real price, but it buys a rehearsed abort path, a working repo at every step, and a natural place to sweep for the B-cdf6 comparison-literal regression class.

preMortem.scenario: The state-dir git mv completes but story archives become unreadable because a hardcoded path was missed.
preMortem.trigger: A .lattice literal outside the resolver, or a path assembled by string concatenation the resolver cannot intercept.
preMortem.consequence: 344 story archives inaccessible; audit history effectively destroyed even though the files are still on disk.
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-002 routes every literal through one resolver, acceptance being that grep finds no bare literal outside the resolver definition. CHK-008 rehearses apply-then-revert on a scratch clone first. CHK-003 acceptance requires story_get to succeed on two archives from different eras, named in evidence.

preMortem.scenario: storyFilesHash turns out to include file PATHS, so the rename shifts it for every story and invalidates freshness bindings wholesale.
preMortem.trigger: The hash is computed over relative paths rather than content only — recorded as an explicit UNKNOWN in understanding, not yet resolved.
preMortem.consequence: Every story with recorded evidence needs rebinding; DONE gates across the repo start failing for reasons unrelated to their own work.
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-001 must resolve this BEFORE CHK-003 runs and record the answer plus chosen handling (accept drift versus add a rebind step). CHK-003 is gated on CHK-001 and CHK-008.

preMortem.scenario: The rename breaks the CANONICAL name while the deprecated one keeps working — the exact inversion B-cdf6 hit four times.
preMortem.trigger: A comparison, regex, allow/deny membership check or ownership predicate that hardcodes the deprecated literal instead of consulting the resolver.
preMortem.consequence: Silent misbehaviour rather than loud failure: config appears to load and policy appears to apply, but the new identity is ignored.
preMortem.mitigation: Sweep specifically for brand literals inside DECISIONS, not just inside output, since that is where all four B-cdf6 regressions lived. CHK-007 flips the residue gate to forbidden so a regression fails loudly. Reviewers get an explicit instruction to hunt this class.

preMortem.scenario: Removing bin/lattice.js breaks a teammate with no warning.
preMortem.trigger: CHK-006 executes without the announcement half, or before the rest is green.
preMortem.consequence: A teammate merging their branch hits command-not-found with no explanation available at the point of failure.
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-006 is sequenced last, acceptance requires a CHANGELOG entry naming both removed aliases and their replacements, and PLAN must explicitly choose and record warn-then-remove versus immediate cut. Per the product reviewer the changelog is the floor, not optional.

preMortem.scenario: The npm package rename silently disarms an external gate keyed on the old package name.
preMortem.trigger: Something outside packages/*/src resolves @lattice/core by exact string — for example pre-push self-repo detection.
preMortem.consequence: A safety gate becomes a no-op without failing, so a later push bypasses a check nobody notices is gone.
preMortem.mitigation: The INIT reviewer verified .githooks/pre-push:155 was preemptively widened by B-cdf6 to accept BOTH names, so that path is safe. CHK-005 must still grep for other exact-name consumers before renaming and re-run verify-entrypoints afterward.
